rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı derives züber as the plural of zübre, a large iron mass; Kāmûs also gives zübre the meaning anvil.
rows.anchor: “Züber”, “zübre”nin cem‘idir. “Zübre” büyük demir kıt‘ası demek olup Kāmûs’ta mezkur olduğu üzere örs mânasına da gelir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reads the two ṣadafs as opposing heads or slopes, possibly the two ends of the barrier or the joining sides of its iron masses.
rows.anchor: iki sadef karşılıklı iki baş veya iki yan teşkil eden iki meyl

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some imagine iron fitted with copper rivets among rocks; Elmalılı allows this, but says the wording more strongly depicts an iron-brick structure coated in copper, beyond even modern engineering to reproduce.
rows.anchor: Bunu bazılarının dediği gibi demir kinedli bakır perçinli kayalardan müteşekkil bir binâ gibi anlamak mümkin olabilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although ancient metallurgy may have managed such a vast heating operation, Elmalılı finds a miracle by Dhu al-Qarnayn or a representation of future technical progress more apparent; collective assistance supports the latter reading.
rows.anchor: İhtimal, fakat bunu ya müfessirînin dedikleri gibi Zülkarneyn’in bir mucizesi telâkkī etmek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The barrier’s unscalable, unpierceable strength exceeds other crossed mountains and breached fortifications; its secret was the poured liquid, a divine force rather than ordinary matter.
rows.anchor: Demek ki bunun sırrı Zülkarneyn’in döktüğü mâyi‘de idi. Demek ki o, alelâde bir madde değil, ilâhî bir kuvvet idi.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhu al-Qarnayn calls the structure neither the people’s work nor his own, but a favor granted solely through divine grace.
rows.anchor: Yani ne sizin işinizdir ne benim, mahza ni‘met-i ilâhiyeden bir inâyet-i rabbâniyedir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The barrier has a term: when God’s promise comes He will level it, and that promise is true, making the Resurrection certain.
rows.anchor: ve Rabbimin vaadi haktır. Kıyamet muhakkaktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı links the promise to 21:96: Gog and Magog will emerge, the earth’s order will be corrupted, and the Resurrection will occur.
rows.anchor: Ye’cûc ve Me’cûc çıkacak, nizâm-ı Arz fesad bulacak, kıyamet kopacaktır

rows.speaker: bazıları
rows.claim: Some identify the barrier with the Great Wall of China and consequently imagine Gog and Magog as Mongols and Tatars; Elmalılı rejects the identification because the wall was crossed and does not match the Qur’anic description.
rows.anchor: Bazıları bunu Sedd-i Çin zannetmişler ve binâen‘aleyh Ye’cûc ve Me’cûc’un Moğollar ve Tatarlar olduğunu tevehhüm eylemişlerdir.

rows.speaker: bazıları
rows.claim: Others identify it as the Iron Gate barrier and place Gog and Magog in present-day Russia; Elmalılı says it is ruined and likewise fails to match the description.
rows.anchor: bazıları da Demirkapı Seddi demişler ve binâen‘aleyh Ye’cûc ve Me’cûc’u bugünkü Rusya sahasında tasavvur eylemişlerdir ki bu da harab olmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No known barrier, including either proposed wall, matches the Qur’anic features; Elmalılı favors a reading of the rampart as the requesting people’s social formation, a material and spiritual defense formed from hard elements by divine effusion.
rows.anchor: Doğrusu Kur’an’daki evsâf ikisine de muntabık olmadığı gibi, diğer yerlerde mâlum olabilen sedlerin de hiçbirine uymuyor.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the people were Turks as commentators report, the passage signals their past work in protecting the earth from corruption and their later service to Islam.
rows.anchor: burada Zülkarneyn’e kuvvetle yardım eden Türklerin mâzîde Arz’ı fesaddan kurtarmak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this conditional Turkish reading, their decline would mean the Gog-and-Magog barrier’s collapse and the earth’s disorder, a sign of the Hour.
rows.anchor: Türklerin inkırâzı, Ye’cûc ve Me’cûc seddinin yıkılması ve nizâm-ı Arz’ın fesâdı demek olacaktır ki eşrât-ı Sâ‘at’tendir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı calls this divinely merciful rampart Dhu al-Qarnayn’s greatest work and says its collapse would bring humanity a great calamity.
rows.anchor: en büyük işi, mahza bir rahmet-i rabbâniye olan bu redmin inşâsıdır ki, yıkılması yeryüzünde beşeriyetin pek büyük bir felâketi olacaktır

rows.speaker: Nizamüddin Hasen Nîsâbûrî
rows.claim: Nîsâbûrî says human beings contain a perfection attainable through cultivation and guidance; the perfected human alone merits vicegerency, and Dhu al-Qarnayn spans spirit and body while mastering causes.
rows.anchor: Nizamüddin Hasen Nîsâbûrî Garâibü’l-Kur’an ve Regāibü’l-Furkân nâmındaki tefsirinde buraya müte‘allik te’vîlât-ı sûfiyeden olmak üzere

rows.speaker: Nizamüddin Hasen Nîsâbûrî
rows.claim: In the allegory, Dhu al-Qarnayn’s westward journey is the human spirit’s sun setting into nature and bodies; the people there are bodily faculties and earthly souls.
rows.anchor: Nizamüddin Hasen Nîsâbûrî Garâibü’l-Kur’an ve Regāibü’l-Furkân nâmındaki tefsirinde buraya müte‘allik te’vîlât-ı sûfiyeden olmak üzere

rows.speaker: Nizamüddin Hasen Nîsâbûrî
rows.claim: The command to punish or treat gently allegorizes disciplining faculties that misuse their purpose; the faithful receive union as their good reward and ease after annihilation and struggle.
rows.anchor: Nizamüddin Hasen Nîsâbûrî Garâibü’l-Kur’an ve Regāibü’l-Furkân nâmındaki tefsirinde buraya müte‘allik te’vîlât-ı sûfiyeden olmak üzere

rows.speaker: Nizamüddin Hasen Nîsâbûrî
rows.claim: The eastward journey represents the rising of the rational soul’s sun after it sheds bodily attachments.
rows.anchor: Nizamüddin Hasen Nîsâbûrî Garâibü’l-Kur’an ve Regāibü’l-Furkân nâmındaki tefsirinde buraya müte‘allik te’vîlât-ı sûfiyeden olmak üzere

rows.speaker: Nizamüddin Hasen Nîsâbûrî
rows.claim: The two barriers symbolize the world of livelihood and civilization and the arena of bodily well-being; the nearly speechless people are ignorant commoners.
rows.anchor: Nizamüddin Hasen Nîsâbûrî Garâibü’l-Kur’an ve Regāibü’l-Furkân nâmındaki tefsirinde buraya müte‘allik te’vîlât-ı sûfiyeden olmak üzere

rows.speaker: Nizamüddin Hasen Nîsâbûrî
rows.claim: Gog and Magog symbolize varied natural powers corrupting humanity by misusing its faculties; the people offer payment and self-sacrifice for a spiritual barrier.
rows.anchor: Nizamüddin Hasen Nîsâbûrî Garâibü’l-Kur’an ve Regāibü’l-Furkân nâmındaki tefsirinde buraya müte‘allik te’vîlât-ı sûfiyeden olmak üzere

rows.speaker: Nizamüddin Hasen Nîsâbûrî
rows.claim: Dhu al-Qarnayn’s call for strength means focused spiritual resolve; iron masses are firm faculties or ironlike hearts, from cradle to grave, and bellows signify continual remembrance and litanies.
rows.anchor: Nizamüddin Hasen Nîsâbûrî Garâibü’l-Kur’an ve Regāibü’l-Furkân nâmındaki tefsirinde buraya müte‘allik te’vîlât-ı sûfiyeden olmak üzere

rows.speaker: Nizamüddin Hasen Nîsâbûrî
rows.claim: Molten copper symbolizes pouring love and steadfastness into hearts, so Satan’s stratagem cannot enter and nothing apart from the Merciful can prevail over them.
rows.anchor: Nizamüddin Hasen Nîsâbûrî Garâibü’l-Kur’an ve Regāibü’l-Furkân nâmındaki tefsirinde buraya müte‘allik te’vîlât-ı sûfiyeden olmak üzere

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bahr denotes the sea generically, meaning all seas as a class.
rows.anchor: Cins-i bahr, bütün cinsiyle deryâlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Midād originally means something by which another thing is extended, but in common usage it specifically means writing ink.
rows.anchor: “Midâd”, fi’lasl bir şeyin uzatılmasına medar olan şeyin ismidir. Fakat örfte yazı yazılan mürekkebe mahsus olmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Lord’s words are the words of divine knowledge and wisdom; they are infinite, while the sea and any finite addition to it remain finite and cannot equal the infinite.
rows.anchor: çünkü kelimâtullah nâmütenâhî, denizler mütenâhîdir. Mütenâhîye mütenâhî zammının mecmû‘u da mütenâhîdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is only human and does not claim to encompass all God’s words; what he has received in revelation is that the audience’s God is one God.
rows.anchor: yani Allah teâlâ’nın cemî‘-i kelimâtını ihâta edemem, öyle bir iddiada bulunmuyorum.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Liqā can mean reaching God’s presence, escaping His reckoning and attaining reward, finding His approval, or longing to see His beauty.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın huzûruna varmak, hesâbından kurtulup sevâbına ermek, rızâsını bulmak veya cemâlini görmek arzu eyliyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One who hopes for meeting the Lord should perform a sincere deed worthy of that meeting and avoid both overt association and hidden shirk such as ostentation.
rows.anchor: Ne yukarıda geçtiği üzere Allah’ın âyet ve likāsına küfredenler gibi şirk-i celî, ne de riyâ gibi bir şirk-i hafî karıştırmasın.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı calls the close of al-Kahf a strong foundation and elegant preparation for the transition to Maryam.
rows.anchor: Sûre-i Kehf’in bu hâtimesi Sûre-i Meryem’e intikal için ne büyük bir esas, ne güzel bir temhid olmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kāf Hā Yā ʿAyn Ṣād is a name of the sura, while its intended meaning is known to God.
rows.anchor: Kâf hâ yâ ayn sâd, bu sûrenin bir ismidir. Murâdını Allah bilir.

rows.speaker: Resûlullah
rows.claim: A report transmitted through Umm Hani says the Prophet glossed the letters as Kāfī, Hādī, yā ʿĀlim, Ṣādık; Elmalılı notes the report’s reliability is not established.
rows.anchor: Ümmühânî’den Resûlullah’ın şöyle buyurduğu mervîdir: “Kâfî Hâdî’sin yâ Âlim-i Sâdık.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı cites ʿAlī’s prayer using the letters and infers that they may be among God’s names.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Ali’nin de يَا كۤهٰيـٰعۤصۤ اِغْفِرْ لِي diye dua ettiği

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is said to have assigned each letter as an allusion to a divine name, such as al-Kabīr or al-Karīm.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan da her harfin Kebîr, Kerîm

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No fixed lexical meaning is established by conventional signification; rational interpretation admits countless possibilities, so the letters are among the ambiguous matters.
rows.anchor: Hâsılı delâlet-i vaz‘iye ile lisânen bir mâna sâbit değildir. Delâlet-i akliye ise lâyu‘ad vücûha muhtemil olabilir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possible symbolic reading maps Kāf to Zechariah, Hā to his wife, Yā to John, ʿAyn to Jesus, and Ṣād to Mustafa, summarizing the sura.
rows.anchor: kâf Zekeriyyâ’ya, hâ zevcesine, yâ Yahyâ’ya, ayn Îsâ’ya, sad Mustafa’ya remz olarak sûrenin mazmûnunu bir icmal olmak muhtemil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possible reading takes Kāf as divine words, Hā as divinity, Yā as certainty, ʿAyn as knowledge, and Ṣād as truth, summarizing the close of the previous sura.
rows.anchor: kâf kelimâta, hâ lâhûta, yâ yakīne, ayn ilme, sâd sıdka remz olmak suretiyle evvelki sûrenin âhirini bir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The letters’ benefit is to show how unaided reason flounders among possibilities and to warn of its inability to grasp higher truths, an ordeal called ibtilā-yı rāsiḫīn.
rows.anchor: Fâidesi de kendi kendine bırakılacak olan aklın ihtimâlât içinde nasıl çırpındığını göstererek metâlib-i âliyeyi idrakte mertebe-i acz ü hayretini ihtardır.

none: This segment contains only the verse-by-verse translation, with no separate commentary point.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The referent is Jesus, the servant born and speaking those words from the cradle onward; Elmalılı renders him as Jesus son of Mary, the word of truth.
rows.anchor: İşte budur öyle doğan ve o sözleri söyleyen bir kuldur tâ beşikten ba‘sine kadar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seven verses with a different rhyme ending are set apart within the sura; Elmalılı says they state its central decision: deny divine sonship, glorify God, and call to monotheism.
rows.anchor: bu âyetler, bu sûrenin asıl maksadını anlatan karar âyetleridir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The declaration that God is Lord of Jesus and the audience continues Jesus’s earlier statement that he is God’s servant and parallels 3:51.
rows.anchor: bu âyet, tâ yukarıdaki إِنِّى عَبْدُ ٱللَّهِ cümlesine mâtuftur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı notes the saying also appears in the extant Gospels and gives the essence of Jesus’s prophetic mission by explicitly affirming monotheism.
rows.anchor: Eldeki İncillerde dahi mezkur olan bu söz, onun nübüvvetinde davetinin hulâsası olduğu ve tevhîdi tansis eylediği

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says Jews and Christian factions differed about Jesus; the following distinct Christian positions are among the views he reports.
rows.anchor: Yahudîler bir türlü söyledi, Nasârâ fırkaları da türlü nizâ‘lara düştüler

rows.speaker: Nasârâ fırkaları
rows.claim: One Christian position calls Jesus the son of God.
rows.anchor: Nasârâ fırkaları da türlü nizâ‘lara düştüler; kimi “Allah’ın oğlu” dediler

rows.speaker: Nasârâ fırkaları
rows.claim: Another Christian position says God Himself descended to earth and then ascended to heaven.
rows.anchor: Nasârâ fırkaları da türlü nizâ‘lara düştüler

rows.speaker: Nasârâ fırkaları
rows.claim: Another Christian position identifies Jesus as one of the three.
rows.anchor: Nasârâ fırkaları da türlü nizâ‘lara düştüler

rows.speaker: Nasârâ fırkaları
rows.claim: Another position says Jesus is God’s servant and prophet.
rows.anchor: Nasârâ fırkaları da türlü nizâ‘lara düştüler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says Ghayy is the punishment for transgression; an unnamed view identifies it as a valley in Hell from which every valley seeks refuge, and the expression Ghayyā pit is familiar in Turkish.
rows.anchor: Azgınlığın cezâsı bir şerre çatacaklar. Denilmiş ki cehennemde öyle bir vâdidir ki bütün dereleri ondan isti‘âze eder, “gayyâ kuyusu” lisânımızda da meşhurdur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated taqī ending recalls Maryam’s earlier story; as Gabriel spoke there, Gabriel’s speech will follow here as well.
rows.anchor: Burada işbu تَقِيًّۭا fâsılasının tekerrürü tâ yukarıda Meryem kıssasında geçen تَقِيًّۭا fâsılasını hatırlatır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spirit who told Maryam he was her Lord’s messenger is Gabriel, and here he answers Muhammad’s question about why he visits less often.
rows.anchor: Orada Meryem’e إِنَّمَآ أَنَا۠ رَسُولُ رَبِّكِ diyen rûh, yani Cebrâil burada Resûlullah’ın bir suâline cevâben demiştir ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening waw is resumptive, and the verse answers a question whose occasion is known from the reports about its revelation.
rows.anchor: Buradaki vâv, istînâfiyedir. Yani bir suâle cevaptır ki bu sual, sebeb-i nüzûlünden mâlum olabiliyor.

rows.speaker: Resûlullah
rows.claim: Elmalılı cites Ahmad, Bukhari, Tirmidhi, Nasa’i, and others: Muhammad asked Gabriel why he visited less often, and this verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem “yâ Cibrîl, bizi ziyaret ettiğinden daha çok ziyaret etmeye ne mâni‘oluyor?” demişti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı takes the verse as Gabriel’s answer; the occasion and content support this, as does the repeated taqī ending recalling Gabriel as the spirit mentioned earlier in the sura.
rows.anchor: Demek ki bu âyet, Cebrâil’in o suâle cevâbını hikâyedir.
